PUBLIC COMMENT
Citizens wishing to address the City Council and Successor Agency on any item on the agenda or on any matter
not on the agenda may do so at this time. State law (Government Code Section 54950 et seq.) prohibits the City
Council from taking action or engaging in discussion on a specific item unless it appears on a posted agenda .
Upon request, the City Council may, in their discretion, allow citizen participation on a specific item on the agenda
at the time the item is considered by the City Council. If you wish to address the City Council /Successor Agency
at this time, please complete a speaker's card and give it to the City Clerk prior to commencement of the City
Council meeting. Please limit your remarks to three (3) minutes.

To increase the effectiveness of the Public Comment Period, the following rules shall be followed: No person
shall make any remarks which result in disrupting, disturbing or otherwise impeding the meeting.

Pursuant to Section 54957.95 of the Government Code, the presiding member of the legislative body conducting
a meeting, or their designee, is authorized to remove, or cause the removal of, an individual for disrupting the
meeting. Any such removal will be preceded by a warning to the disruptive individual by the presiding member of
the legislative body or their designee that the individual ’s behavior is disrupting the meeting and that the
individual’s failure to promptly cease their disruptive behavior may result in their removal.

  CONSENT CALENDAR
Items under the Consent Calendar are considered to be routine and may be enacted by one motion. There will be
no discussion of these items unless members of the Public or City Council request specific items to be removed
from the Consent Agenda for a separate discussion. lf the item is desired to be discussed separately, it should be
the first item under Scheduled Matters.

AGENDA ITEMS AND ACTIONS
5:00 P.M. CLOSED SESSION

CALL TO ORDER Mayor Argumedo called meeting to order at 5:02 p.m.

ROLL CALL

PUBLIC COMMENT ON CLOSED SESSION ITEMS There were no individuals wishing to address the City Council on any items on the Closed Session agenda.  

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION City Council /Successor Agency recessed to Closed Session at 5:03 p.m.

RECONVENE TO OPEN SESSION City Coiuncil/Successor Agency reconvened to Open Session at 6:00p.m.

ORAL CLOSED SESSION ANNOUNCEMENT City Attorney Tapia stated that regarding item #6 on the regular agenda regarding employment agreement for City Manager position, staff prepared Resolution and contract and copies are provided to the City Clerk for the public.  

City Attorney Tapia reported on Closed Session items #1, #2 and #3.  Staff made a presentation, City Council provided direction and no reportable action was taken on those items.  


6:00 P.M. - CITY COUNCIL MEETING

CALL TO ORDER

ROLL CALL

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

INVOCATION

APPEARANCES AND PRESENTATIONS

1.. Proclamation Designating the Month of April 2024 as “Autism Awareness Month.” Parks and Recreation Director Alaniz delivered a brief presentation before introducing Commissioner Mariam Madrigal. Commissioner Madrigal then addressed the audience, shedding light on the experiences of children with disabilities, particularly their sensitivities to stimuli like noise. She emphasized the crucial need for City staff and Deputies to undergo specialized training in effectively supporting and managing individuals with disabilities.




2.. Proclamation Designating April 7-13, 2024 as “National Library Week” Library Director Bautista provided an overview of the library programs planned for the Library week.   Mayor Argumedo read the proclamation. 

PUBLIC COMMENT There were no individuals wishing to address the City Council on any items within their jurisdiction. 




CONSENT CALENDAR  -  Action: approve (Pass) Moved by Oralia Rebollo

3.. Approval of Warrant Register Nos. 16A, 16B, and 16C

SCHEDULED MATTERS

9.. Capital Improvement Program Update for FY 2023/2024  -  Action: approve (Pass) Moved by Mireya Garcia Deputy Director of Public Works, Nila, delivered a summary of the staff report. Conversation ensued regarding the citywide street lighting master plan, including the City Council's potential input on light selection and other recommendations. Deputy Director Nila noted that most lights are owned by SoCal Edison, and they dictate the specific lights used.

4.. Second Amendment to the Professional Services Agreement with Nelson/Nygaard, Inc.

8.. Award of Construction Contract to Armstrong Cal Builders, Inc. for the Bandini Library and Learning Center Project  -  Action: approve (Pass) Moved by Kevin Lainez

7.. Slauson Corridor Median Landscape Improvements Concept Plan  -  Action: approve (Pass) Moved by Kevin Lainez Deputy Director of Public Works Operations Nila gave a concise overview of the staff report. Greg Garces from KOA Corporation outlined that the project spans 2.7 miles, with 50% of the corridor featuring raised median improvements. They've engaged in outreach with local businesses affected by the additional median installations.

A representative from Nuvis Landscapes highlighted their collaboration with the City arborist, proposing various trees and plants to enhance the area's aesthetics, including seasonal flowers and year-round foliage.

The conversation addressed concerns raised by businesses regarding the impact of raised medians on U-turn access to their properties. Mayor Argumedo emphasized the safety benefits of raised medians in reducing accidents caused by left turns in those areas.


10.. A Status of the City’s Recruitments -- Follow-up  -  Action: approve (Pass) Moved by Kevin Lainez Acting City Manager Domic presented a summary of the staff report, noting that the YES program is currently underway. In response to Councilmember Lainez's inquiry about the contract Permit Technician, Acting City Manager Domic mentioned that the individual would join the team next Monday. Councilmember Lainez suggested conducting a live video lottery on Facebook for the YES Program.

The discussion then shifted to recruitment for Parks and Recreation positions.


CITY COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY REPORTS Councilmember Garcia shared that the "Crown Day! Unlock Your Future" event on April 4th was a resounding success, offering empowerment and motivation to the young women in the community.

Additionally, Councilmember Garcia acknowledged the Library Commissioner's positive report on a well-executed library program and commended the Library Director for their exemplary work. She also proposed two agenda items for the next Council meeting: the Business Watch Crime Prevention Program and an overview of Code Enforcement processes and timelines.

Councilmember Rebollo expressed gratitude for the collaboration on "Crown Day! Unlock Your Future" with Melissa Demirichi, and extended thanks to Transtech, Lavarez Glassman and Colvin, and CalWater for their sponsorship. Councilmembers Lainez, Vice Mayor Altamirano, and Mayor Argumedo congratulated Councilmembers Garcia and Rebollo on the success of the event. Vice Mayor Altamirano suggested considering a similar event tailored for young men.

Mayor Argumedo shared insights from a meeting with the Director of Transportation and Acting City Manager regarding transportation issues, announcing the introduction of a new bus that could potentially halve travel time and serve previously underserved areas.

Mayor Argumedo also attended a Sanitation District meeting and clean-up day, expressing gratitude to all participants and sponsors for their efforts in cleaning the entrance to I-5. Over 20 volunteers participated, and Caltrans was commended for their follow-up cleaning on the other side of the road.


ADJOURNMENT A meeting adjourned at 7:30 p.m.

Written materials distributed to the City Council are available for public inspection immediately following the posting of this agenda (at least 72 hours prior to a regular City Council meetings) in the City Clerk's Office, at Commerce City Hall, 2535 Commerce Way, Commerce, California, and the Central Library, 5655 Jillson Street, Commerce, California.

Meeting facilities are accessible to persons with disabilities. ln compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) if you need special assistance to participate in this meeting, notify the Office of the City Clerk at (323) 722-4805 at least 24 hours prior to the meeting.

5.. PRESENTATION/UPDATE FROM THE SHERIFF'S DEPARTMENT OF PUBLIC SAFETY IN THE CITY OF COMMERCE Sergeant Duarte presented a summary of the statistics from the past two weeks, highlighting ongoing efforts by deputies to address homeless encampments within the City.

6.. Employment Agreement for City Manager Position  -  Action: approve (Pass) Moved by Oralia Rebollo City Attorney Tapia announced that Ernie Hernandez is the proposed candidate for the City Manager position, and there is an agreement on the table for the City Council to review and consider.
